Differential testing depends on independent implementations: agreement can miss a preprocessing bug shared by training, export and deployment. Practical implication: supplement parity checks with small, independently derived golden fixtures specifying raw inputs, expected token IDs, padding/masks and output interpretation; avoid generating expectations through production preprocessing. Metamorphic testing adds checks without requiring exact prediction labels, but relations must follow the model’s actual contract—for example, batch permutation should preserve corresponding predictions under deterministic inference. Research on ML classifiers shows that ordinary cross-validation can miss implementation faults detected by metamorphic checks. [ML classifier testing study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3082144/)

Mutation testing assesses whether checks detect deliberately injected faults. Confirm that each mutation reaches an applicable execution path, changes an intermediate value and can affect an asserted result; an unexecuted mutation provides little evidence about oracle strength. Distinguish surviving non-equivalent mutants from genuinely equivalent changes and behavior left unspecified. Run identical checks against the unchanged implementation as a clean control, with fixed randomness and justified numerical tolerances, to identify false alarms. Report fault detection alongside clean-control failures and mutation applicability. These are practical design implications; ML mutation-testing research cautions that mutation realism and the distinction between production and test behavior require scrutiny. [Reachable-mutant study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07348), [critical reflection on ML mutation testing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01341)
